inputs.text: Medium waist-up photograph at eye level, 35mm lens. A fictional adult woman in her thirties with a light chestnut chin-length softly waved bob looks down at a brass compass she holds out in front of her chest with both hands, the open dial facing the camera. She wears a mustard-yellow canvas field coat with flap chest pockets, metal buttons and shoulder tabs, and a chunky teal cable-knit scarf. The compass is large in the frame, about as wide as her palm: a round polished brass case with its hinged brass lid open behind it, a clear glass cover, and a cream dial printed with four large bold black capital letters, N at the top, E on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left, a black degree tick ring around the edge, and one straight needle with a red north half pointing at N and a silver south half pointing at S. All four letters N, E, S, W and the red needle are sharp and clearly readable. She stands beside a weathered wooden potting bench in a rain-soaked Victorian greenhouse with a dark green painted window grid, rain droplets on the glass panes and potted ferns.
